sources.entry: SwiftPlantUML - Generate and view class diagrams from Xcode for Swift code. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/MarcoEidinger/SwiftPlantUML-Xcode-Extension) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A macOS app and Xcode/Finder extension that generates PlantUML class diagrams from Swift code, built on the SwiftPlantUML Swift package.
summary.what_it_does: SwiftPlantUML.app generates a class diagram for Swift code, either from inside Xcode or from the Finder. In Xcode it can create a diagram from the current Swift file or from selected Swift code, and the README mentions an "Open editable diagram in browser" command. In Finder it can create a diagram from one or more selected Swift files. The hosting macOS application is used to configure the diagram visualization. The Source Editor Extension and Action extension both rely on the SwiftPlantUML Swift package. For large diagrams spanning many folders, the README recommends using SwiftPlantUML as a command-line tool instead.
use_cases: Generate a class diagram for a Swift file in Xcode
Diagram selected Swift code inside Xcode
Create a class diagram from Swift files via Finder context actions
Visualize class relationships in a Swift project
Produce large multi-folder Swift diagrams from the command line
how_to_run: Alternatively: download the latest SwiftPlantUML package from the Releases page
Copy SwiftPlantUML to your Applications folder
Enable the Xcode Source Editor extension in System Preferences > Extensions > Xcode Source Editor > SwiftPlantUML
Enable the Finder extension in System Preferences > Extensions > Finder > Open Swift Class Diagram
notable: Runs SourceKitten work in a sandboxed XPC service so the Xcode extension can be distributed via the App Store
Works both as an Xcode Source Editor extension and as a Finder extension
Can also be used as a command-line tool for large, multi-folder projects
caveats: Xcode extension initialization may take around 30 seconds on first launch; the README suggests checking Console for XPC crash reports if the prompt does not appear within 60 seconds
If Xcode is installed outside /Applications/Xcode.app, the xcode-select path must be adjusted to avoid a sourcekitd loading failure
Large diagrams across many folders are recommended to be generated with the command-line tool rather than the app
